name: Northwest Ridge
beta: From the high pass south of the Birdwood Lakes, turn onto the northwest ridge and follow it up. The lower half is a loose, exposed scramble that most parties find stays near Class 3. Higher up the ridge steepens and narrows, with a short knife-edge and a few harder moves in the 5.4-5.5 range; rock quality is poor, so test every hold. Many parties carry a rope, a small rack and slings for the harder steps.
overview: The Northwest Ridge is the more commonly used route up Birdwood, ahead of the harder Lizzie's Ridge on the southeast side. It starts from the long Commonwealth Creek trail to Smuts Pass and then follows a narrow, airy crest of loose limestone to the summit.

current.approach: Park at the road end near Mount Engadine Lodge off the Smith-Dorrien Trail, then follow the Commonwealth Creek trail through forest and meadow to Smuts Pass. Bears are common in the valley, and the trail is hard to follow where an avalanche brought down trees.
current.descent: Descend the northwest ridge the way you came, then return along the pass and valley trail to the road.

name: Southwest Ridge
beta: Above the tarns, cross a faint headwall right to left, follow the glacial stream to a shallow col, and cross the snowy plateau to the ridge. The crux is two narrow notches in the ridge, each downclimbed and then climbed out of the far side at about 5.4. Fixed anchors and large boulders allow a rappel station if you want to protect them. Past the notches, a plain hike leads to the top.
overview: The Southwest Ridge is the main route up Cline, a long approach with a small bivy site at alpine tarns and a ridge with two deep notches as the technical highlight. After the notches the summit is a straightforward walk.

current.approach: Park on the grassy area across the David Thompson Highway from Thompson Creek Campground. Follow the creek trail about 4 km, crossing twice on logs, then climb the west moraine gully, a flagged route over a cliff band on a treed ridge, and a long scree slope past twin waterfalls to the tarns.
current.descent: Return by the ridge, downclimbing or rappelling the notches, then retrace the approach to the highway.

name: "A" Crack
beta: Begin up and to the right of the neighbouring Blow Fly line and follow the thin crack past an old piton to reach a bolt on the face. From there the face continues leftward and a little higher, with a runout, until you meet the fourth bolt of that neighbour and finish up it.
overview: A slim crack passes a piton to a bolt on the face; the line then angles slightly left across the face to merge with its neighbour at the fourth bolt and finishes there. Poorly protected, hence the X.

current.descent: scramble off via the gully toward Bobcat Boulder, or down slopes right of Gender Blender
current.location: Above and beyond Blow Fly's Last Ride on its right-hand side

name: Arizona 7
beta: Begin just to the right of the neighbouring route on the left and climb the face, clipping two bolts, to a flake, then step left into the prominent crack. Follow it beside a small roof, trending back right above the roof to a fixed piton in a second crack, and finish up the face to the top.
overview: Starts up the face with two bolts to a flake, then goes left into a prominent crack beside a small roof, crosses above the roof to a fixed pin in another crack, and finishes on the face.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Fixed Line Traverse
beta: The first pitch is shared with Doug's Dandy. On the second pitch, shift a bit south and pull the overhang, then scramble rightward and higher to a slim ledge heading south. On the third, traverse past a bolt and choose among a handful of variations to the summit area, then scramble east to the top of the Head.
overview: Shares its first pitch with Doug's Dandy. Pitch two shifts slightly south, climbs an overhang (5.6), then scrambles right to a narrow ledge leading south. Pitch three crosses past a bolt and takes whichever variation suits (5.2) to the summit area.

current.area_walk_in: The canyon sits up on the Head and is entered by climbing one of the Boulder Canyon routes beneath it.

name: Banana Crack
beta: Share the start with Two Cams & Jam and follow the wide, right-curving crack until it flattens out horizontally. At that point leave it and climb directly up the face, going over the zenolith, to the top.
overview: A wide crack that arches to the right until it turns horizontal. The line then leaves the crack and heads straight up the face over a zenolith.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Shares the start of Two Cams & Jam

name: Birthday Girl
beta: Begin next to Bubblenutz on its right and move rightward over a small roof onto a smooth slab and into a corner and up the face above. For the short corner, bring a few stoppers plus cams to roughly 2 inches.
overview: Trends rightward over a little roof onto a smooth slab, enters a short corner and finishes on the face above; mostly bolts with a little gear.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.detailed_rack: Bolts plus a few nuts and cams up to 2 in to protect the short corner
current.location: Starts immediately right of Bubblenutz and works up and rightward

name: Black Streak
beta: Begin below and to the left of Gravity and climb the obvious dark streak to bolts on the right. Continue up the face past those bolts to a thin crack, then follow the crack to the top.
overview: Named for the dark streak it follows at the start. The climbing begins on the face past bolts and finishes in a thin crack.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: about 60 feet down and left of Gravity, up the dark streak

name: Blow Fly's Last Ride
beta: Begin around the corner up and to the right of Young Monkeys, and follow the horizontal crack leftward until you are just right of the prow. Then climb the face rightward, clipping three bolts, to the fourth, continue right to the fifth, then drift left toward bolt six, and finish by heading rightward and above the seventh bolt to the top.
overview: Often called the best route on the mountain: traverse a horizontal crack left toward the prow, then wander up a bolted east-facing slab, right, left and right again, to the top.

current.descent: scramble off via the gully toward Bobcat Boulder, or down slopes right of Gender Blender
current.location: Up and around the corner to the right of Young Monkeys, at a horizontal crack

name: Blue Highways
beta: Start on the right-facing flake just left of the left-facing dihedral and climb it to a horizontal crack, watching for an owl that may be nesting. Then step right into a thin crack and follow it to the top, where the hardest moves are.
overview: Climb the flake to a horizontal crack, then step right into a thin crack that holds the crux to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Beside a dihedral whose corner faces left, where a flake faces right

name: The Far Side
beta: The first pitch begins by scrambling to the foot of a short dihedral, which you climb to a sequence of roofs. Work through the roofs to a stemming section, then layback to the belay. Loose rock is likely, and gear can be fiddly to place.
overview: A two-pitch line up the left-hand wall of the Ladybug buttress. A short dihedral leads through overhangs to a stemming section and a layback. The rock is loose and gear can be awkward.

current.location: in the left-hand wall of the Ladybug buttress, about 70 ft along the hikers' gully

name: Brusin' and Cruisin'
beta: Work up and leftward over easy ground to a flake and climb the right side of it until you can move out left and higher to the two-bolt belay, the same belay that tops the first pitch of Hanging Gardens. Climb the face above for a full rope length with one bolt along the way to reach the top.
overview: The route offers a choice of style on its first pitch: wrestle it as an off-width or layback the flake. A short easy face pitch with one bolt leads to the top.

current.location: shares its start with Hanging Gardens

name: Camel's Foot
beta: Start on the south side of the pinnacle and climb that side directly to the summit, clipping the single bolt on the way.

current.area_walk_in: Reached by walking up a ramp that runs beside the canyon's right edge.
current.descent: single-rope rappel off the north side
current.location: South side of the small pinnacle

name: Cary'd Away
beta: Start at the right end of the wall and climb the face, clipping a single bolt, then follow a seam by two horizontal cracks and a boulder that is perched there. This brings you under a hand crack, and a short face section above gets you to the top.
overview: A bolt on the face, a seam crossing two horizontal breaks and a boulder wedged in place, then a hand crack and a brief face finish.

current.area_walk_in: Loose soil and rock below these crags makes walking up damaging and sometimes dangerous, so anchors are placed on top. Gear up above, descend by rope to the base, then climb back up to your packs.
current.descent: single-rope rappel
current.location: Right-hand section of a varnished wall divided into thirds by two chimneys, up on the saddle's north end

name: Catch the Wave
beta: Plan on bringing two long ropes, about 165 feet each, to rappel back down to the ledge after finishing.
overview: An outstanding, sustained bolted line on the north face; descending requires a double-rope rappel to the ledge.

current.descent: double-rope rappel (two 50 m ropes) down to the ledge

name: Changes in Attitude
beta: Step right from the small boulder onto the face and climb past a pair of bolts and a horizontal crack to a two-bolt belay. Expect a bit of a runout, on easy terrain, near the top.
overview: A short face climb up a boulder sitting over Dark Passage, with a horizontal crack midway. Easy ground near the top has some runout.

current.area_walk_in: Head east on the Marcus Landslide trail for roughly a third of a mile, then turn right at the Sven Slab sign. Loop around a big boulder and over a low rise, then pick up the climbers' path on the right toward the Nit Nat flake. Many informal tracks dead-end in brush; if you are squeezing through thick scrub, turn back.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Chase the Dragon
beta: The first pitch follows the obvious crack on aid, clipping aid bolts to a small ledge above an overhang. The second continues up the crack with free and aid moves, clipping four bolts, to a sling belay. Then traverse right on a ledge past a bolt to a stance, and finish up a ramp angling rightward to the summit. A variation exits left from the sling belay.

current.location: Middle of the north face of the formation

name: Cholla Traverse
beta: Share the start with North Central Variation. The first pitch traverses right to a hanging belay on two bolts, and the second goes straight up for around sixty feet, clipping three bolts, to a good ledge. The third pitch continues rightward.
overview: A multi-pitch route that works rightward across the wall on bolted belays. The name hints at prickly trouble but the climbing is moderate.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Shares the start of the North Central Variation, then traverses right to a hanging belay

name: Coriolis
beta: Find the line a short way right of Wormsign and ascend a run of broken flakes that face left to reach the bolted slab above.
overview: Broken left-facing flakes lead up to a slab protected by bolts; one of the most travelled pitches on the formation.

current.area_walk_in: Descend the gully used for the Reef of Rocks, then follow the wide ledge that cuts across the formations. A short third-class step around a corner brings Aegir into view; keep along the ledge to the foot of the routes.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: About 15 ft right of Wormsign

name: Cowpunks
beta: The route starts on the face and then moves to an arete. Near the top it is awkward to stay on the arete, since easier-looking terrain lies leftward, yet the bolts are on the arete itself.
overview: Face climbing leads to an arete. Holding the arete near the top is awkward, since the climbing is simpler off to one side, whereas the bolts sit on the arete itself.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Dead Meat
beta: Start low and to the right of Loafer's Choice and climb the face to a bolt beneath a roof. Get over the roof, then climb the face using the leftmost crack until you can step out left onto the arete and follow it to the top.
overview: A sustained route that starts on a bolted face, goes through a roof, and finishes up an arete. It never really lets up, so treat the grade with respect.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Below and to the right of Loafer's Choice

name: Deep Freeze
beta: Step off the flake onto the face to enter the vertical crack and follow it past a bolt, where unusual pocket moves lead to a last bulge. Get over the bulge via the crack, then continue up the face past two bolts, trending left to the top.
overview: Rated among the finest routes in Phoenix: a long vertical crack with pocket climbing, a bulge, and a face above. It was among the early hard free leads of its era, about 160 feet long.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.detailed_rack: Bolts, stoppers, and cams up to 3 inches.
current.location: About 25 feet right of Succubus; step from a flake onto the face to enter a vertical crack

name: Birdland
beta: Pick the left-hand flake, the one with the whitewashed tip, and climb the south face of the flake past its bolts to the top. To get off, scramble down and to the right.
overview: Climb the south face of the left-hand flake, which has a pale-stained tip, past bolts to the top.

current.descent: scramble off toward the right
current.location: left-hand flake with a white-stained tip

name: Dog Fight Giggle
beta: Start a short way right of Black Streak and layback the flake up to a ledge, which holds the hardest moves. Continue up the right-facing corner, clipping one bolt, then finish in a thin crack to the top.
overview: A lieback flake leads to a ledge, then a right-facing corner with a bolt, and finally a thin crack to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Around 20 ft further along from Black Streak, on the right

name: Doug's Dandy
beta: Start at a granite outcrop around the middle of the east wall and scramble to a large ledge beneath an overhang. Next, shift south a few feet and pull the overhang, then scramble to a belay bolt. After walking north to a big saguaro, traverse north past bolts and an overhang to a buttress, climb it to a belay, and take gullies east to the summit.

current.area_walk_in: The canyon sits up on the Head and is entered by climbing one of the Boulder Canyon routes beneath it.
current.location: Begins at a granite outcrop about halfway along the east wall of the canyon

name: Crispy Dudes
beta: Look for the small amphitheater in the middle of the rock, with a decayed arch at left and a gentle off-width on the right. Work a bit up the arch, then go leftward by a bolt to a horizontal break and go on up beyond several additional bolts to a hanging belay on two bolts. On the second pitch, get out under the overhang to either side.
overview: The centre of the rock holds a small amphitheatre: a decayed arch to one side, an easy-angled wide crack to the other. Climb the arch briefly, step across, clipping a bolt, to reach a horizontal break, then continue clipping further bolts to a hanging stance on double bolts. The second pitch leaves under the overhang in either direction.

name: Beat the Drummond Slowly
beta:
Begin in the shallow corner twenty feet right of East Face. The second pitch heads up and rightward into an overhanging corner, and the third returns rightward to an amber-colored wall and a horizontal break that ends at a belay with two bolts.

On the final pitch step left, climb flakes past an old bolt ladder, traverse leftward to the overhangs, and pass them with a swing and a touch of aid.
overview: The first belay is on a ledge reached up the corner, and the second pitch takes an overhanging corner. The third heads back right across an amber wall to a horizontal break and a two-bolt belay. The final pitch passes an old bolt ladder and loose flakes, then traverses left under overhangs to a bolt-assisted swing and A0 move over the roof.

current.location: 20 ft over from the East Face line, in a shallow corner that faces right

name: Breathairian
beta: Begin up a chute that takes little gear, and past a bulge move left to an arch that faces left. Where the arch steepens, exit right by a thin crack, turn another bulge and follow demanding face moves to a shelf where you belay. The second pitch goes leftward to a mantle over a poor landing, then climbs a corner and a steep jug-filled face to the ramp, which is the way off.
overview: Climbs a chute with poor protection, trends left after a bulge to an arch that faces left, and leaves it by a thin crack on the right into hard face climbing and a shelf belay. Pitch two has a 5.10-R mantle onto a poor landing, a right-leaning corner, then steep jugs to the ramp.

current.descent: scramble off along the ramp
current.location: 20 ft over from Fractured Fairy Tales, up a chute with poor protection

name: Easy Chair
beta: Walk about fifty yards west from behind Hanging Gardens, then go up the slab that faces east, clipping its two bolts.
overview: A slab climb on an east-facing wall, with two bolts for protection.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Energizer
beta: Start at the left end of the boulder's face and climb the face and arete, clipping two bolts, to the top. Get down with a single-rope rappel.
overview: A short bolted route on a big three-sided boulder sitting in a hollow below Sven Slab. It combines face and arete climbing, and a harder variation starts just to its right.

current.descent: single-rope rappel
current.location: left side of the west-northwest face of the triangular boulder

name: Facer's Choice
beta: Start below the east end of the wall at a big boulder pile. Scramble right out of the ledge full of bushes to a large crack and a clear face. Climb the east face to the knife-edged top, then traverse left to get down.
overview: An east-facing route up a large crack and a clean face to a knife-edged top. It is a fine warm-up, especially in winter.

current.descent: traverse left along the top and descend
current.location: below the east end of the wall at the big boulder pile

name: Feel the Creep
beta: This route is entered from above. Cross the slab to the anchor, rappel down, and then climb back up the thin face, clipping four bolts. Expect long smearing moves rather than holds.
overview: Rap in, then climb thin, smeary face protected by four bolts. A smearing test.

current.area_walk_in: Loose soil and rock below these crags makes walking up damaging and sometimes dangerous, so anchors are placed on top. Gear up above, descend by rope to the base, then climb back up to your packs.
current.descent: Rappel in from the top anchor, then climb back up
current.location: Roughly 30 ft beyond Just Fine; the rappel anchor sits over on the slab higher than Just Fine's rap bolts

name: Alice's Restaurant
beta: The first pitch climbs the face to a bolt, then continues until it clips the final bolt of Bugati Cafe's opening pitch, and ends on the little ledge where you belay. The second pitch heads almost directly up the face over the belay along four bolts spaced in a row to the summit.
overview: A two-pitch face route on the south side of the first spire, joining Bugati Cafe's opening pitch and then heading directly to the summit up a line of bolts. Run out in places.

current.location: adjacent to the starting crack of Harcourt Fenton, to its right, short of the treed alcove

name: Four Flakes (Three Turks)
beta: Climb the face, clipping four bolts, to the stance on the shoulder over your head. After that you just walk off, which may feel like easy scrambling.
overview: A short bolted face low on the spire's left side, about forty feet along from Don't Bug Me's start. It ends on the shoulder, and the descent is a walk.

current.descent: walk off; likely class 3
current.location: lower-left part of the spire, about 40 ft from where Don't Bug Me begins

name: Fly By
beta: Scramble easy fifth class for about twenty feet to the anchor bolts, rappel down, and then climb back up the face left of the gully, clipping four bolts to return to the anchor.
overview: The most northerly climb at this crag, set on a big dark brown boulder at the end of the trail. It is a short bolted face climb reached by rappelling in first.

current.area_walk_in: Loose soil and rock below these crags makes walking up damaging and sometimes dangerous, so anchors are placed on top. Gear up above, descend by rope to the base, then climb back up to your packs.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Northernmost route of the group; anchor sits on a big dark-brown boulder east of the trail's end

name: Child of Troubled Times
beta: Step from the boulder onto the face, then pull a tricky unprotected move onto a solid foothold to get at a bolt. From there climb the face into a crack and follow it past a fixed piton to the top.
overview: Step from the boulder onto its face, make a tricky unprotected move to a good foothold and a bolt, then follow a crack past a fixed piton to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Sits on a large boulder's northern side, in a gully crossed on the way up to the cliff base

name: Neil's First Piece
beta: Share the start with the Standard Route, but where that route cuts across to the left onto easier terrain after the crux, go directly upward, clipping two bolts.
overview: Shares its beginning with the standard line but rises directly, clipping two bolts.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Grin & Bear It
beta: Start on the southeast face and climb the face with two bolts to a roof, then get over the roof, clipping another bolt, to reach the top.
overview: Bolted face to a roof, over it, and on past one more bolt to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: On the southeast face

name: Gripple Variation
beta: Begin immediately right of the original start, mid-face, and climb to a bolt, then move up and left on the face to join the regular route.
overview: A harder alternative start to Energizer, beginning farther right in the middle of the face and later rejoining the original line.

current.descent: single-rope rappel
current.location: just right of the original start, middle of the face

name: Hanging Mantle
beta: Start at the left end of the wall below an overhang and climb over it, then continue up the face to a flake. At the flake's top, traverse right beyond a bolt and go up the face to finish.
overview: A short face climb near the left end of the wall that begins by getting past an overhang, then finishes with a traverse right across a flake to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Far southwest end of the wall, beneath the overhang
